@graph.name: Tray Palletizer
@graph.description: A tray palletizer is a robotic system that stacks loaded trays, such as bakery, dairy or meat trays, onto pallets in a stable pattern, using tooling selected for the tray format and weight. TRF Industrial Automation builds tray palletizers on TRFCobot, TRFCompact and TRFSpeed, or as a custom palletizer, and the right model is defined by your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Can a Tray Palletizer Work in a Freezer or a Chilled Room?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. For palletizing areas below 32°F, TRFSubzero is the TRF palletizer built for frozen food, ice cream and other below-freezing areas. For a chilled room above freezing, send TRF the room temperature so the application can be evaluated. In every case, rate, payload and tooling are validated per application.

mainEntity.name: Can One Tray Palletizer Handle Several Tray Formats?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. Each format and pallet pattern is stored as a recipe, so the operator selects the pattern at changeover. The practical limits are the tooling's ability to hold every format securely, the robot's reach at the tallest stack and the number of pallet positions the layout allows, all confirmed during project engineering.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Tray Palletizer and a Tray Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tray packer loads packaged trays into shipping cases; a tray palletizer stacks trays, or the finished cases, onto pallets. They sit in different parts of the line and often work together: a case packer packs the trays, a case palletizer builds the pallet of cases, and conveying connects them.

mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for Loaded Trays?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the loaded tray plus the tooling, and for multi-tray picks, the combined weight of the trays. Published case weights are up to about 22 lb for TRFCobot, 44 lb for TRFCompact and 66 lb for TRFSpeed. TRF validates the payload with your heaviest loaded tray and evaluates a custom palletizer above that range.

mainEntity.name: Can a Tray Palletizer Be Used in a Protein Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for packaged trays and crates. Packaged trays move between machines on TRFIntraflow, and palletizing below 32°F points to TRFSubzero. Sanitary conveying for exposed product upstream is evaluated per application with TRFCleanflow. Each application is validated with the plant's tray formats, cleaning routines and room conditions.

mainEntity.name: How Much Does a Tray Palletizer Cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost depends on the platform, rate, loaded tray weight, tooling, pallet positions, pallet handling and the conveying around the cell. As a reference, list prices are US$ 120,000 for the TRFCobot Dual, US$ 180,000 for the TRFCompact Dual and US$ 350,000 for the TRFSpeed 100, EX Works Lenexa, Kansas, installation not included. The robotic palletizer cost page explains each factor.

mainEntity.name: What Information Should I Prepare to Size a Tray Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your tray and crate formats with dimensions, the loaded weight of the heaviest format, trays per minute at peak, shifts per day, the room conditions (chilled, frozen or washdown), stacking rules and a drawing of the floor space. A TRF Sales Engineer uses this data to screen TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or a custom palletizer, and the payback calculator gives a first estimate.
